text:
Colorado arrives stung and Montreal arrives hot. The Avalanche lost 4-3 in overtime at Ottawa two days ago, with Shane Pinto scoring the winner after the Senators trailed in the third, and they're 2-1-2 in their last five without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. The Canadiens beat Boston 5-2 to end the Bruins' four-game winning streak, have points in twelve straight (9-0-3), and are missing Ivan Demidov and Chris Kreider.

The numbers say the teams are close. At five on five, Colorado has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Montreal 51%, and our model has it 3.42 to 2.95 for the Avalanche. The special-teams matchup is Colorado's power play, at 0.81 expected goals a game, against a Montreal penalty kill that allows 0.82, with the Canadiens taking about five penalties a night. In net, projected starter Mackenzie Blackwood sits at +1.0 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots deserved), while Jakub Dobes is at -6.0 this season after +17.3 last year.

Nathan MacKinnon is our top Colorado pick, 38% to score and 82% for a point. For Montreal, Cole Caufield (36% to score) carries a five-game point streak, and with Demidov out he has moved beside Juraj Slafkovský and Alex Newhook. Our under-the-radar picks are Gabriel Landeskog, with 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games from third-line minutes, and Nazem Kadri, 58% for a point. Both are players to watch, not locks.
